title: Report the number that was measured
statement: Report every result as measured on real output, misses included and never rounded across its bar, recomputed from primary records; a projected, templated or summary-copied figure is no result.
example: A calibration set cited as having about 150 responses had 48.
detail: Audits of an assessment's approval case found summary tables showing reliability as "0.930 ✅" against a ≥0.93 benchmark where the reports beneath them said 0.928, and the one failing metric (RMSE 4.12 vs <4.0 target) left out of every summary table (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_AUDITS_AND_FIXES.md`). A red-team pass on a writing course's package found a reused calibration set cited as "48 items, ~150 banded kid responses" that was 12 items and 48 responses, a number inherited from a research agent's summary and not recomputed before it was written down (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/RED_TEAM_R1.md`), and one grade's certified count drifted 541 vs 549 vs 559 across documents. The course plans' rules since: every number carries a source and comes off one dated pull, no magnitude is carried from another grade or cohort, one grade's bars and yields need a recalibration set before they gate another, and an unknown cell is marked [TO SOURCE], never invented (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/course-formula-agents.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/grade-band-profiles.md`). Never round a near miss across its bar, leave out a failing metric or copy a number from a summary, and mark a number not yet measured as unsourced.
against: One rosier summary and one metadata slip don't show that summaries usually drift rosier, and in the judge calibration the recomputed numbers matched the harness's own (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0243-generator-quality-schema-cluster-2026-07.qmd`). The code check has false positives on numbers stored in another form ('## Known false-positive: R3 on 0.9 pass rates', `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/feedback_use_claim_validator_before_save.md`, line 88). The per-run decision tables in the same folder were computed from each run, so the fault was in the templated narrative rather than in every count.
